links.outcome: Optimal protocol selection by LLM versus radiologists' human-selected protocols on the same cases
links.effect: GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more often than humans (96.2% [527/548] vs 88.3% [484/548]; P < .001); inappropriate protocols 1.3% vs 2.4%, P = .21.
links.quote: GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more frequently than humans (96.2% [527 of 548 patients] vs 88.3% [484 of 548 patients]; P < .001), but there was no evidence of a difference in inappropriate protocols (1.3% [seven of 548 patients] vs 2.4% [13 of 548 patients]; P = .21).

links.outcome: Reference standard defined by radiologists and blinded radiologist review of protocol categories
links.effect: Reference standard protocols were set by radiologists with institutional guidelines; outputs were categorized by blinded radiologists. Effectiveness of the practice itself was not tested.
links.quote: Model-selected protocols and original human-selected protocols were categorized compared with the reference standard after review by blinded radiologists as follows: exact match, equal alternative, reasonable but inferior, or inappropriate.

unlisted_practices: Context engineering with detailed prompt instructions versus fine-tuning to optimize LLM protocol selection
Comparison of LLM performance by training level of the human protocoler (resident, fellow, radiologist)

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance (prompting vs fine-tuning) against radiologists for CT scan protocoling on a retrospective dataset, but does not test an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
